rows.citation: Rotter, S., Diesmann, M. (1999). Exact digital simulation of time-invariant linear systems with applications to neuronal modeling. Biological Cybernetics, 81(5-6), 381-402.
rows.model_type: time-invariant linear ODE systems; integrate-and-fire neurons with linear subthreshold dynamics (numerical integration method)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - proposes an exact matrix-exponential integration scheme; no edited models or fault mutants are generated.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - scheme accepts a general input class including delta-pulse trains; no designed battery of current-clamp protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - compares solvers by error in subthreshold dynamics and spike timing; no eFEL-style feature set.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no stimulus or test-set selection; the comparison concerns integration schemes.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - performance analysis against multi-purpose solvers; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI or automated model edits.
rows.software: none named in abstract (full text not accessed)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Supplies exact reference solutions for linear subthreshold dynamics, useful background for trustworthy reference traces and step-size effects. NeuroSem's conductance-based NeuroML fixtures are nonlinear, so it calibrates tolerances by h, h/2, h/4 refinement instead; no behavioural-drift testing here.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (api.crossref.org/works/10.1007/s004220050570: title, 2 authors, Biol Cybern 81(5-6):381-402, 1999); Europe PMC REST search by DOI (PMID 10592015) for abstract. Full text paywalled, not read.

rows.citation: Blundell, I., Plotnikov, D., Eppler, J. M., et al. (2018). Automatically Selecting a Suitable Integration Scheme for Systems of Differential Equations in Neuron Models. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 12, 50.
rows.model_type: integrate-and-fire neuron ODE systems described in NESTML for the NEST simulator (solver selection toolbox)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - analyses model equations to choose a solver; no deliberate faults or mutants are introduced.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - symbolic and numeric ODE analysis (propagator eligibility, stiffness test); no current-clamp protocol battery reported.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - criteria are analytic solvability and stiffness, not spike or voltage features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - automates choice among analytic propagator, explicit and implicit schemes, not stimulation protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - stiffness tester applied to all NESTML neuron models as validation (reported non-stiff by default); no held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no - automation is symbolic (SymPy) and numeric (GSL), not AI-driven edits.
rows.software: ode-toolbox https://github.com/nest/ode-toolbox (GPL-2.0 per GitHub API; PyPI odetoolbox 3.0.0 on 2026-09-13)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Chooses solvers per model; it does not test behaviour preservation after edits. NeuroSem treats solver/step changes as a numerical mutation family and checks divergence against refinement-calibrated tolerances; this toolbox could help anticipate stability-breaking solver mutants.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (api.crossref.org/works/10.3389/fninf.2018.00050: 4 authors incl. Morrison, article 50, 2018-10-08); Europe PMC abstract (PMID 30349471) and full text XML (PMC6186990) for implementation section; GitHub REST api.github.com/repos/nest/ode-toolbox (license, description); PyPI JSON pypi.org/pypi/odetoolbox/json.

rows.citation: Prinz, A. A., Bucher, D., Marder, E. (2004). Similar network activity from disparate circuit parameters. Nature Neuroscience, 7(12), 1345-1352.
rows.model_type: three-cell conductance-based model of the crustacean stomatogastric pyloric network (large parameter-space simulation)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - systematically varies synaptic strengths and intrinsic properties across over 20 million combinations; parameter sweep, not single-fault mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - abstract describes network output activity only; no stimulation battery evident (full text not accessed).
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - network activity patterns compared for similarity; specific feature definitions not verified from full text.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection of stimuli or tests.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - exhaustive simulation database; no held-out evaluation design.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Foundational motivation: near-identical output can arise from very different parameters, so one observation can mask parameter changes. NeuroSem turns this into a testing problem, using stimulus batteries to expose parameter mutants that a canonical test misses.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/nn1352: 3 authors, Nat Neurosci 7(12):1345-1352, online 2004-11-21); Europe PMC REST abstract (PMID 15558066). Full text paywalled, not read.

rows.citation: Marder, E., Goaillard, J.-M. (2006). Variability, compensation and homeostasis in neuron and network function. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 7(7), 563-574.
rows.model_type: review of theoretical and experimental neuron and network studies (invertebrate and vertebrate)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - narrative review of parameter variability and compensation; no mutants or edits generated.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - abstract does not discuss stimulation protocols (full text not accessed).
rows.electrophysiology_features: unclear - abstract concerns tuning of synaptic and intrinsic currents, not a feature-extraction method.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no test or stimulus selection.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Conceptual background on multiple parameter solutions producing similar behaviour, supporting why a single canonical test is weak. It proposes no testing method; NeuroSem contributes the operational mutation-calibrated, multi-protocol detection pipeline.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/nrn1949: 2 authors, Nat Rev Neurosci 7(7):563-574, 2006); Europe PMC REST abstract (PMID 16791145). Full text paywalled, not read.

rows.citation: Alonso, L. M., Marder, E. (2019). Visualization of currents in neural models with similar behavior and different conductance densities. eLife, 8, e42722.
rows.model_type: single-compartment conductance-based bursting neuron models (custom Python code, RK4 at 0.1 ms; not NeuroML)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - graded decrease and complete removal of each maximal conductance across six models; perturbation analysis, not recorded single-fault software mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - constant current injection sweeps plus conductance-decrement perturbations; no step, ramp or rebound protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - ISI distributions, spike and burst detection, membrane-potential distributions and currentscapes; custom definitions, not eFEL.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - perturbations are illustrated, not selected; a genetic algorithm only searches model parameters.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - six hand-selected models from 1000 generated bursters; no held-out split.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest in rationale: models alike at baseline respond differently to perturbations. It is visualization for insight; NeuroSem adds mutant classification, refinement-calibrated tolerances, greedy protocol selection and held-out model and mutation-family evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (api.crossref.org/works/10.7554/elife.42722: 2 authors, eLife 8 e42722, 2019-01-31, abstract); Europe PMC full text XML (PMC6395073) for methods, perturbations and data availability; DataCite API api.datacite.org/dois/10.5061/dryad.d0779mb.

rows.citation: Gutenkunst, R. N., Waterfall, J. J., Casey, F. P., et al. (2007). Universally Sloppy Parameter Sensitivities in Systems Biology Models. PLoS Computational Biology, 3(10), e189.
rows.model_type: 17 systems biology ODE models (mostly SBML from BioModels); biochemical, not neuronal
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - Hessian-based sensitivity to continuous parameter variation; no discrete single-fault mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - each model analysed under several experimental conditions chosen by original authors; biochemical conditions, not electrical stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - species time courses and chi-squared cost, not electrophysiological features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - optimal experimental design mentioned as related separate work, not performed here.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - survey across a model collection; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.software: SloppyCell https://github.com/GutenkunstLab/SloppyCell (BSD-3-Clause per GitHub API; paper cites sloppycell.sourceforge.net)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Explains why many parameter changes barely affect outputs, which bears on equivalent-mutant rates and on not treating every change as a defect. NeuroSem instead empirically tests neuron-model edits with stimulation batteries and calibrated tolerances.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (api.crossref.org/works/10.1371/journal.pcbi.0030189: 6 authors, PLoS Comput Biol 3(10) e189, 2007-10-05); Europe PMC abstract (PMID 17922568) and full text XML (PMC2000971) for model collection and SloppyCell mention; GitHub REST search for SloppyCell repo; HTTP check of sloppycell.sourceforge.net (200).
